### Invariants and traps

1. Register every new test twice. A suite without a `test:*` script and a link in the `test` chain (`tests/package.json:9`) never runs in CI; helpers are deliberately unregistered. The chain stops at the first failure, so fix the earliest red suite first.
2. Server suites hang, not fail, without `FLOWS_TEST_SANDBOX=1` in this sandbox (worker-server.mjs:14-L19, L163). Silence until a timeout is not a red assertion.
3. `flows-weight` has 0.2-0.9 KiB of headroom on every route except login (2.4 of 5 KiB) (computed today: ticker 399.1/400, overview 264.4/265, strategy 250.1/251, market 241.5/242, desk 233.8/234, side and watch 217.8/218, unusual 203.8/204, ask 172.1/173, track 163.3/164, history 156.7/157, events 154.8/155, political 143.6/144). Any byte added to `flows-ui.js` (105.3k, on every route), `flows-rt.js` (32.1k), `flows-fresh.js`, `flows-dock.js` or a page controller probably fails `flows-weight.mjs:12-27`. The test message says "raising the ceiling is a decision and should look like one in the diff"; the alternative is a reclaim elsewhere. A new `*Page` function without a `CEILING_KIB` entry fails, a stale entry fails (L94-L99).
4. `flows-reads-contract` fails any new `path === "/api/flows/<x>"` route in `worker.js` that has no `CEILING` row and is not in `HOME` (L801), so price new routes in rows (index search = rows returned, scan = whole table, `json_each` over a payload = array length), not only in trips. A query that stops using its primary key shows at once. The D1 read cap is 5,000,000 rows/day (AGENTS.md; DEPLOY.md 10.4b).
5. Repository-wide "source carries no comments" is enforced by tests in two places. `flows-rt-contract.mjs:1421-1429` fails any line matching `^\s*//` or containing `/*` in `shared/flows-rt.js`, `shared/flows-rt-hub.js`, `shared/flows-rt-routes.js`, `tests/rt-fixtures.mjs`, `tests/flows-rt-contract.mjs` and `tests/flows-rt-server.mjs` (the `/*` test also trips a `"/*"` inside a string or regex, and a URL like `http://` is fine only because it is not `//` at line start). `flows-strip.mjs` proves `scripts/strip-comments.mjs` is idempotent and parseable on every `assets/js` file; `scripts/strip-comments.mjs` is described in AGENTS.md as a no-op that stays only for a possible build command, yet this test imports `stripComments` and `stripTree` from it, so it cannot be deleted without changing the test.
6. Source scans pin literal text. `flows-rt-contract.mjs:1438-1447` requires `export { Pulse } from "./shared/flows-rt-hub.js"` and `path.startsWith("/api/rt/")` in `worker.js`, and the exact `[[durable_objects.bindings]]` / `[[migrations]]` adjacency in `wrangler.toml`; the rt modules may not contain the words INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE (after removing `Update`), `env.AI`, `.run(`, `UW_ONDEMAND` or `console.log|warn|info|debug` (L1432-L1435). `flows-starts-contract.mjs:35-L62` pins `flows-live.yml` byte patterns (permissions block `contents: read / id-token: write / actions: write / issues: write`, `FLOWS_LIVE_KEEP`/`FLOWS_LIVE_LOOP` "1", the `drill` boolean input and `flows-live-drill` concurrency group, exactly two `uses:` both `actions/(checkout|setup-node)@<40 hex>`, no secret other than `UW_API_KEY` and `FLOWS_INGEST_URL`) and `flows-pipeline.yml` (no `issues:`, exactly one `actions: write`, an `origin` input naming `live-loop`); it also executes the nightly's gate step extracted by regex, so renaming that step breaks it. `flows-ticker-contract.mjs:203-L212` requires the pipeline to still contain `const shed = [` and the entry shape `["name", "dropped to fit`, and every shed name to be a registry panel. `flows-universe-contract.mjs:241` requires `scripts/flows-legs/focus.mjs` to import `../../shared/flows-live.js` and `../../shared/flows-focus.js`. `flows-reading-worker.mjs:338-L341` requires `shared/flows-reading-worker.js` to contain no `.AI.run(` and exactly one `askModels(` call site handed `deps.ai()`, and `worker.js` to build that dep with exactly one `ai: () => cappedAi(` (every model call goes through the meter). `flows-sign.mjs` requires no two-armed sign in any `assets/js/flows-*.js` and a CSS rule for every neutral class a page emits.
7. Count-coupled constants break on honest changes: `CHECKS_ON_CLEAN = 13` (flows-warnings.mjs:83) when a warning check is added/removed; `bank.items.length === 106` (mastery-contract.mjs:20) when the review bank is regenerated; the 15/3/3/3/3/3 and 5/5/5 placement balance and `.placement-method-grid a` count of 7 (placement-contract); the 12-course `TOPICS`, `SLUGS`, `PAGES` and stage counts (`regression.mjs:8-24, 164-165`); `MODULES` (ten ticker modules, ticker-contract.mjs:174) and `TICKER_PANELS` registry; `ARCHETYPES` (six) and the 22-tag table in flows-reading; `RT_TOPIC_KEYS` order and the 25 px columns in flows-rt-contract.
8. Date traps. Fixed fixture dates (2026-09-xx) are used with a shifted `Date` (`shiftClock`) because a card two sessions behind the real date is tier `expired`; a new fixture with a fixed session needs the same shift (`flows-reads-contract.mjs:121-L131`, `flows-reading-worker.mjs:22-L23`). `flows-strategy.mjs:23-L50` derives its expiries from the real clock (`prevTradingDay(easternDay(Date.now()))`, third Fridays, a Friday-search fallback), so it is the one suite whose inputs move with the calendar. `flows-rt-server.mjs` measures real time (13 s idle wait, 60 s production-cadence window) and is wall-clock sensitive on a loaded machine; `flows-rt-client.mjs` pauses the page clock (`pauseAt`) because an installed clock keeps running otherwise.
9. `flows-strip.mjs:73-L79` regenerates `tests/.review-emit/` only when no `-card-*` file exists there; a stale directory (one is present here from 2026-09-24) means the strip test renders old cards and can mask a pipeline change. Delete the directory to force a fresh emit. `flows-ticker-contract` and `flows-unusual-contract` always delete and rebuild their own emit dirs, so a failing `--dry-run` there surfaces as a crash at import time (`execFileSync` with `stdio: "ignore"`, no message).
10. Node requirements: `node:sqlite` needs Node >= 22.13 and the `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning` script flag; `flows-rt-contract.mjs:34` calls `process.threadCpuUsage()` with no fallback (live-stubs.mjs:141-L148 falls back to `hrtime`), so an older Node fails that suite at the first CPU probe. CPU ceilings are timed in-process and can flake on a loaded machine (flows-rt-contract L1157 under 25 ms/poll; flows-reading CPU under 6 ms; reading-worker hit under 25 ms / miss under 60 ms).
11. Node-imported Worker needs shims: `globalThis.HTMLRewriter`, `globalThis.caches.default`, and a fresh `worker.js?tag=N` per client so module memos (`memoClock`, single-flight maps, schema bootstrap) do not leak between cases. `flows-reads-contract` runs with `FLOWS_READ_MODE: "off"` (client() L134) and filters `flows_dossier_cache` trips (`isReadingTrip` L165) so reading traffic is priced separately in its final block; keep that when adding routes.
12. Test secrets: `FLOWS_SESSION_EPOCH:1` is passed to workerd while `wrangler.toml` sets `"2"`; every workerd suite signs sessions with epoch `"1"` (`signSession({..., epoch: "1"})`, `signFlowsSession(user, secret, ttl, "1", 0)`). The production value in `wrangler.toml` is not what the tests exercise. `FLOWS_ASK_MODEL` is blank so no workerd suite reaches a model; never expect `llm: true` from `startWorker`.
13. `placement-contract` is not a Worker test: it stubs `/api/v2/bootstrap`, `/api/bootstrap` and `/api/me` itself, so a change to those payloads is not caught there (it is caught in `regression.mjs` mocks and `worker-regression`).
14. `regression.mjs` and `worker-regression.mjs` encode Lab behaviour that AGENTS.md no longer describes (12 courses, v2 API, challenge, projects, five learning paths). When changing the Lab, read these two files, not AGENTS.md.
15. `worker-regression` hits `/cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled?cron=&time=` with the real cron strings from `shared/flows-live-worker.js` (`HOUSEKEEPING_CRON`, `SUMMARY_CRON`); changing a cron expression requires changing `wrangler.toml`, `flows-rt-contract` L1446 and these constants together.
16. Port and process hygiene: every `startWorker` boot is its own wrangler process group; a crashed test run leaves nothing only if `armSweep` handlers ran. `flows-worker-contract` boots six, `flows-rt-server` four, so these are the slowest suites and the first to time out under load; in sandbox mode each boot re-copies the whole tracked tree.
17. `tests/package.json` is the only place chain order lives; AGENTS.md's runtime numbers are point measurements and drift (e.g. it quotes 123 s for `flows-pipeline-contract`, Tests B notes the same).
18. `worker-regression.mjs` asserts the asset cache policy (`/assets/css|js|fonts/*` immutable with or without `?v=`, the two version tokens one hour, missing file answered by the asset layer's `404.html` under the path's policy and no CSP, L215-L268) through `wrangler dev`, which only applies it because the root `_headers` file is in the served directory. What is actually asserted: css/js/fonts immutable with and without `?v=` and on a 304 (L215-L244), the two version tokens `assets/version.txt` and `assets/fonts-version.txt` at `public, max-age=3600` (L245-L253), and the 404.html answers for missing css/js/fonts (L260-L268); the `/assets/img/*` and `/assets/data/*` one-hour rule is in `_headers` but only status and security headers are checked for `/assets/img/og.png` (L234). `.gitignore` un-ignores `_headers`, so `stageServedTree` (tracked + untracked-not-ignored) copies it; an ignored or untracked-and-ignored copy would silently turn these into failures with a baffling `cache-control` diff.
19. Several suites create sibling temp state inside the repo: `tests/.ticker-emit`, `tests/.unusual-emit`, `tests/.review-emit`. They are ignored by `tests/.*/`, but a run killed mid-way leaves them and `flows-strip` will reuse them (trap 9). `flows-universe-contract.mjs`, `flows-record-contract.mjs`, `flows-scores-contract.mjs`, `flows-stock-contract.mjs`, `flows-variation.mjs`, `flows-vol-contract.mjs`, `flows-warnings.mjs`, `flows-sign.mjs`, `flows-weight.mjs`, `flows-ws-probe-contract.mjs` write nothing.
20. `flows-ws-probe-contract.mjs` and the probe it covers must never print the token: the contract asserts the token never appears in any output line (L125), that a refusal never carries the real token (L102) and that the redactor strips both raw and URL-encoded spellings (L82); only key names and statistics are kept.
21. `flows-reading-render.mjs` and `flows-rt-client.mjs` assert that no `innerHTML`/`outerHTML`/`insertAdjacentHTML`/`document.write` string carries model or headline text (INSTRUMENT L29-L100; HOSTILE fixture L55-L57), and `flows-reading-worker.mjs` asserts the reading field stays under 14,000 bytes and the prompt under 7,000 estimated tokens (L483-L486); loosening any of these needs the matching change in the UI or in `shared/flows-reading*.js`.

### How to change it

Pick the row by the module you edit; run its suites plus anything else in the chain that imports the same module (`grep -ln "<module>" tests/*.mjs`). In the sandbox prefix server suites with `FLOWS_TEST_SANDBOX=1` and set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` for Chromium suites; run from `tests/`.

## Appendix: findings, documentation drift and what this map cannot prove

This appendix is the honest edge of the map. Section A lists places where AGENTS.md or DEPLOY.md disagree with the source (the source wins everywhere in this map). Section B lists suspected defects found while mapping; none has been fixed, because the mapping was strictly read-only. Section C lists what only production or the Cloudflare and GitHub dashboards can prove. Section D keeps each chapter author's own notes on what it did not re-verify.

### A. Source versus documentation (source wins)

| Document says | Source says | Where |
|---|---|---|
| AGENTS.md: seven courses and no `/api/v2/*` learning routes | 12 courses, 365 stages, 84 skills; routes `/api/v2/bootstrap`, `progress`, `attempt`, `preferences`, `project`; skill, project and challenge tables and the AI usage tables are created outside `schema.sql` | `92a-lookup-server` rows G05, B06-B10; `12-config-infra` |
| DEPLOY.md: the Worker dispatches the nightly at 17:15 ET (`PHASE_MINUTES.nightlyAfter`) | the only caller is the `*/30` cron, so the first send is 17:30 ET and the retry 18:30 | `90b-flows-data` section 8; `worker.js` dispatch |
| AGENTS.md: the Worker turns D1 error 7500 into `503 store_quota` and serves the last good copy | nightly reads catch the error and answer `store_unreadable`, then serve the last-good copy (`worker.js:995-997, 3997-3999`); `store_quota` is the answer only for errors that escape `route()`, such as ingest writes (`worker.js:4008-4010`); `lk` and `now` have no last-good fallback | `90b-flows-data` section 8; `92a-lookup-server` Q08 |
| AGENTS.md: `focus.mjs` builds the `focus` and `roster` payloads | `focus.mjs` builds only `focus` | `90b-flows-data` section 8 |
| AGENTS.md: `live-day.mjs` runs eight dry days | 13 dry scenarios | `90b-flows-data` section 8 |
| DEPLOY.md: the witness has five checks and a 30-minute chain / `sector:trix` deadline | `WITNESS_CHECKS` has six; the deadline is 36 minutes in source | `90b-flows-data` section 8 |
| AGENTS.md: the review bank has 96 items | `mastery-contract` asserts 106 review items; `REVIEW_ITEM_BY_ID` holds 106 | `92b-lookup-rest`, `62-tests-c` |
| AGENTS.md lists `placement-contract` as needing the dev server | it runs its own static server and never calls `startWorker` | `92b-lookup-rest`, `92c-playbooks` |

### B. Suspected defects (not fixed, read-only mapping)

1. **Skill attempts from variant stages are rejected by the server.** `lab-course.js:211` `recordSkills` sends `st.variantId || st.id` as the item id. 181 stages in `assets/data/courses/*/*.json` carry a `variantId` (challenge, case and match stages, for example `coint-engle-granger-challenge-core`). `validSkillItem` (`worker.js:662`) accepts only `<skillId>:v1|v2|v3`, an id in `REVIEW_ITEM_BY_ID` (106 ids, shaped `course:stage`) or a key of `COURSE_STAGE_BY_ID` (365 keys, shaped `course:stage`). None of the 181 variant ids and none of their plain stage ids is a key of either map, so `PUT /api/v2/attempt` answers 400 `invalid_skill_attempt` (`worker.js:2925`). The local skill record still updates (`auth.js:636` `recordSkillAttempt` saves locally and queues the event). Checked by reading the code and loading the manifests in Node; no request was made and the retry queue's handling of a 400 was not examined. No test covers it.
2. **Anonymous work claimed on a fresh browser may be discarded when the account's server generation is above 0.** Read from source by the `90a-flows-request` author, not executed and not re-checked by me.

### C. What only production or a dashboard can prove

- Which commit is deployed to anilkaya.org, Workers Builds branch mapping and whether a non-production build ends in a version upload that cannot apply a Durable Object migration (`wrangler.toml:33-39`, DEPLOY.md 10.5n).
- Dashboard secrets (especially `GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN`), Transform Rules, WAF rules, custom domains, the `www` GitHub Pages redirect, which Cloudflare plan is in force, billing alerts.
- Live quality of model readings (refusal rate against the vet), rail latency and real hibernation behaviour, vendor quote lag, the production Cache API last-good copy (proven only on local workerd and a Cache API fake).
- Whether the unusual vendor socket is entitled (the probe workflow is dispatch-only and its result is an owner action).
- Owner actions as the session knew them (not derivable from code): vendor licence email, Workers Paid confirmation and billing alerts at $10, $25 and $50, `GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, the 12-members decision (recommendation: add nobody), running the socket probe, deciding whether to publish the roadmap page, a scheduled check on Monday 2026-10-05 15:30 UTC.
